record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: In the bipartite two-measurement d-outcome Bell setting (N, M, K) = (2, 2, d), show that every face of the local polytope C that is not already contained in a face of the no-signalling polytope P is of CGLMP type, possibly after lifting a lower-dimensional CGLMP inequality by fusing outcomes.

evidence.quote: In the setting of problem 26, consider especially the case (N, M, K) = (2, 2, d).

Problem 27.A:
Show that every face of the local polytope C, which is not already contained in a face of the no-signalling polytope P is of CGLMP type, i. e., an inequality of the form first written out in [CGLMP], but possibly lifted from lower dimensions by fusing together some outcomes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the bipartite Bell scenario with two parties, each performing one of M = 2 measurements, where every measurement has K = d possible outcomes. A behavior is specified by the joint probabilities P(a,b | x,y) for outcomes a,b ∈ {0,1,…,d-1} and measurement choices x,y ∈ {1,2}. Let:

• C be the local (classical) polytope, consisting of all behaviors P(a,b|x,y) that admit a decomposition
   P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_λ q(λ) p_A(a|x,λ) p_B(b|y,λ)
with q a probability distribution and p_A, p_B response functions.

• P be the no-signalling polytope, consisting of all non-negative normalized behaviors satisfying ∑_a P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_a P(a,b|x',y) and ∑_b P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_b P(a,b|x,y') for all parameters.

Then C ⊆ P. A CGLMP inequality is the family of Bell inequalities introduced by Collins, Gisin, Linden, Massar and Popescu for arbitrary outcome number d, in the (2,2,d) scenario; a lifted CGLMP inequality is one obtained from a CGLMP inequality in a (2,2,d') scenario with d' < d by partitioning (fusing) the d outcomes into d' groups.

Prove or disprove: every facet of C that is not also contained in a facet of P is, up to relabelling of parties, measurements, and outcomes, a CGLMP inequality, possibly lifted from a lower-outcome CGLMP inequality by fusing outcomes.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved in the negative. In the bipartite scenario with two settings and four outcomes (2,2,4), a complete classification of inequivalent symmetric facet Bell inequalities revealed eight genuinely 4-outcome facets; only one of these is the CGLMP inequality, while seven others are inequivalent to CGLMP (and not liftings of lower-outcome CGLMP inequalities). Thus the (2,2,d) local polytope is not exhausted by CGLMP-type facets, refuting the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Looking for symmetric Bell inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: the list contains the CGLMP inequality, but surprisingly it also contains 7 inequalities that are inequivalent to it, thus answering in the negative Gill's question
status_evidence.claim: In the (2,2,4) scenario, seven facet Bell inequalities inequivalent to CGLMP exist, refuting the conjecture that all non-trivial facets of the (2,2,d) local polytope are CGLMP type.
